correctness.rationale: For B=[[A,I],[I,0]] its inverse is [[0,I],[I,A]] and in characteristic two B+B^-1=diag(A,A); B unipotent iff A nilpotent, equivalent on a finite vector space to all state periods powers of two. On a nilpotent Jordan block J_l(0), determinant of tI-B=(t+1)^(2l), while ker(B+I) is ker A of dimension one, so there is precisely one J_{2l}(1). In characteristic two (I+J)^2^j=I+J^2^j and Fix counts are q^{sum min(2^j,2lambda_i)}, primitive orbit counts by difference/period; B invertible excludes transients. Path continuant f_m=t f_{m-1}+f_{m-2}, f_{2u+1}=t f_u² plus nonzero even constant prove path nilpotence exactly m=2^r−1; independently computed path characteristic polynomials over GF2 n1..20 and checked all such sizes. Cycle S+S^-1=S^-1(S+I)² implies two nilpotent blocks when n=2^r and nonzero eigenvalue otherwise. The claimed path versus cycle maximal period and probabilities then follow from Jordan block length, not finite enumeration.
